goal: VC-200-001 (P1) claims mastery of: P2P Non-blocking Swarm. Its own narrative does not claim delivery: PARTIAL: UDP LAN discovery, TCP JSON-RPC peer dispatch, and trust-score ranking already worked. Closed the routing gap the code itself flagged ("bloom-filters of peer registries for perfect routing"): peers now exchange a real 256-bit `CapabilityBloom` of their registered tool names during ping/pong, and `rank_peers_for_goal` scores peers by goal/capability overlap instead of trust alone (`src/gaw. Prove or refute it: add a nonzero test named vc_200_001_mastery_* that exercises the capability on its production path, and record exactly which part is missing when it cannot be proven. Coverage is not mastery: this closes only when the capability is verified, and a linked closed task is not evidence. Closing this task records the outcome, not a passing test: write .agents/roadmap-verdicts/<the vector>.json with verdict 'delivered' (and the test or record that proves it) or 'not-delivered' (with what is missing and the task ids that track the follow-up work), then run scripts/check-roadmap-verdict.py <the vector> — which is this task's acceptance. A refutation therefore closes the task and files the work, instead of stalling on a test that cannot pass; the roadmap and the queue both understand the record.
title: Verify mastery: Federated Cross-Node Consensus
